body:
version: "1"
kind: miner
id: 4433
slug: livecert
protocol: generic
name: LiveCert — Sourced Answers for Agents
description: >-
  Sourced answers for agents and apps across 36 intents, each read live from a
  named primary source so the caller can check it. Every answer opens with a
  one-sentence answer, then returns the values as fields, the source and the time
  it was checked. Compliance: sanctions screening of people, companies and wallets
  against the OFAC SDN and UN lists with near-match scores; company register
  records (status, company number, register, registered address and agent,
  parents) from GLEIF and SEC EDGAR; SEC filings with acceptance times and each
  10-Q or 10-K's own XBRL figures; URL reputation from Cloudflare and Quad9 threat
  DNS and URLhaus, each source named. Research: question answering with every
  claim cited, web search with dated reports, fact checks with the source URL and
  evidence sentence, and academic, clinical and news search. Markets: prices and
  market data for coins, tokens and listed companies, 10-K revenue and earnings,
  exchange rates and macroeconomic prints (US CPI and unemployment from BLS, the
  federal funds target range from the New York Fed, euro-area HICP from Eurostat
  and ECB rates). On-chain: transfer verification with confirmations and the
  burned base fee, transaction and contract activity across EVM chains, wallet
  balances, gas, token holders and cross-chain messages. Security: live TLS
  certificates, URL scans, CVE records and fraud signals. Weather: forecasts,
  current conditions and storm risk. Also translation, IP geolocation, prediction
  market outcomes, text extraction, sentiment and classification. Only the
  question-answering, sentiment and classification sentences are phrased by a
  model, each with a keyless fallback, and a phrased answer is kept only when every
  claim cites a numbered source; everything else is computed, not generated.
base_url: https://miner-wine.vercel.app

endpoints:
  - path: /ssl-check
    external_path: /ssl-check
    method: GET
    intents: [SSL_VERIFICATION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Is the TLS certificate for github.com valid?", "When does
      example.com's certificate expire?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason,
      checked_at and domain, valid, chain_complete, issuer, valid_to, days_remaining.
      Live TLS certificate check for one domain. Accepts a bare hostname, a full
      URL, or host:port.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: domain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Hostname to check. Accepts example.com, https://example.com/path, or example.com:8443."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The hostname is extracted from it."

  - path: /storm-alert
    external_path: /storm-alert
    method: GET
    intents: [STORM_ALERT]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Is there a storm risk in Chennai in the next 48 hours?",
      "Will gusts exceed 60 km/h in Miami tonight?". Returns answer, verdict,
      confidence, reason, checked_at and location, risk_score, wind_direction,
      max_wind_gust_kmh, max_wind_speed_kmh, max_precipitation_mm, thunderstorm,
      window_hours, valid_at, peak_at, latitude, longitude, threshold_exceeded,
      threshold_hours.
      Severe-weather risk for a location over the next 48 hours. Accepts a place
      name or "lat,lon".
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: location
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Place name, e.g. Chennai or Tokyo, Japan. Provide either location, or lat and lon together."
          - name: lat
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Use with lon when the question names coordinates."
          - name: lon
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180."
          - name: hours
            type: integer
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Forecast window in hours, 1 to 168. Defaults to 48."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Carries wording the structured fields cannot: a point in time such as 'in 44 hours', a wind threshold such as 'above 25 knots', or an operational context."

  - path: /papers
    external_path: /papers
    method: GET
    intents: [ACADEMIC_SEARCH]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Find recent peer-reviewed papers on CRISPR gene editing",
      "Most cited papers on transformer models since 2023". Returns answer, verdict,
      confidence, reason, checked_at and topic, from_date, to_date, papers, count.
      Finds peer-reviewed papers on a topic, optionally within a date range, via
      OpenAlex. Returns title, authors, year and citation count for each.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Research subject to search for, e.g. zero knowledge proofs. A bare topic with no question scaffolding is fine."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Carries constraints the topic alone cannot: a date range, a result count, or a requested ordering."

  - path: /translate
    external_path: /translate
    method: GET
    intents: [LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Translate 'Good morning' into French", "Say hello in
      Spanish". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      source_text, target_language, target_code, translation, source.
      Translates quoted text into a named target language. Returns the
      translation itself, in the target script.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: text
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The text to translate, exactly as given, without surrounding quotes."
          - name: target_language
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The language to translate into, by name or ISO 639-1 code, e.g. Spanish or fr."
        optional:
          - name: source_language
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The language of the source text, when stated. Detected automatically when omitted."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim, e.g. Translate \"Good morning\" into French."

  - path: /ip-geolocate
    external_path: /ip-geolocate
    method: GET
    intents: [IP_GEOLOCATION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Where is 8.8.8.8 located?", "Which network owns 1.1.1.1?".
      Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and ip, city, region,
      country, country_code, latitude, longitude, timezone, asn, organisation.
      Live IP geolocation. Accepts an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a whole question
      containing one.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: ip
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "IPv4 or IPv6 address to geolocate, e.g. 8.8.8.8."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The address is extracted from it."

  - path: /weather-forecast
    external_path: /weather-forecast
    method: GET
    intents: [WEATHER_FORECAST, WEATHER_CHECK]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the forecast for London tomorrow?", "What is the
      weather in Tokyo right now?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason,
      checked_at and location, window_hours, span_days, start_time, end_time,
      hourly_count, temp_min_c, temp_max_c, total_precipitation_mm,
      precipitation_probability_max_pct, max_wind_speed_kmh, precipitation_hours,
      latitude, longitude.
      Current and future conditions for a location. hours=0 reports the present
      hour; any other value gives a window of up to 168h, and the default with no
      hours parameter is 24h. Accepts a place name or "lat,lon".
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: location
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Place name, e.g. New York City. Provide either location, or lat and lon together."
          - name: lat
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Use with lon when the question names coordinates."
          - name: lon
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180."
          - name: days
            type: integer
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Forecast span in days, 1 to 16, e.g. 7 for a 7-day forecast."
          - name: hours
            type: integer
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Forecast window in hours, 1 to 168. An alternative to days."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Carries wording the structured fields cannot, such as an explicit start date like 'starting September 1st' — without it the forecast starts today."

  - path: /extract
    external_path: /extract
    method: GET
    intents: [CONTENT_EXTRACTION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Extract the dates and amounts from this invoice: …". Returns
      answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and extracted.
      Structured extraction from text supplied inline in the question. Reads quantities
      and units, contact details, named entities, action items, dates and events, or
      bare numeric values, and answers with the extracted fields themselves. The text
      is carried in the question, so nothing is fetched and the answer is deterministic
      and checkable against the input.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: text
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The text to extract from, usually quoted after a colon in the question."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. It names which fields to extract, e.g. Extract the contact details from: \"...\"."

  - path: /headlines
    external_path: /headlines
    method: GET
    intents: [NEWS_HEADLINES]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What are today's technology headlines?", "Top business news
      in Europe". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and topic,
      region, headlines, count.
      Current news headlines for a topic and optional region, read live from Google
      News at request time and returned as a numbered list with each source named.
      Honours a requested count such as "top 5". Headlines rotate, so the answer states
      the date it was read.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Subject to fetch headlines for, e.g. technology, business."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Carries the region and any requested count."

  - path: /wallet-balance
    external_path: /wallet-balance
    method: GET
    intents: [WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the ETH balance of vitalik.eth?", "Balance of 0x… on
      Base". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and address,
      chain, balance_eth, symbol.
      Native-coin balance of an EVM address, read with eth_getBalance at the latest
      block from public JSON-RPC on the chain the question names — Ethereum, Base,
      Arbitrum, Optimism or Polygon. A zero balance is reported as zero; an RPC that
      does not answer is reported as unavailable rather than as zero. Token balances
      such as USDT are not included, and the answer says so when one was asked about.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: address
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The 20-byte EVM address to read, e.g. 0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. It names the chain and any token asked about alongside the native coin."

  - path: /tx-lookup
    external_path: /tx-lookup
    method: GET
    intents: [ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP]
    description: >-
      On-chain activity, asked about a transaction or about an address. Example
      questions: "Did transaction 0x… succeed, and who sent it to whom?", "When was
      contract 0x… deployed and how many transactions does it have?". For a
      transaction it returns verdict and a transaction object with status, from,
      to, value_wei, value, symbol, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status,
      method, gas_used, fee_wei, confirmations, base_fee_wei and base_fee_burned,
      which is true on Ethereum and Polygon, where the EIP-1559 base fee is burned,
      and false on rollups, where it is paid to the sequencer. A
      transaction is read by hash from public JSON-RPC on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum,
      Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain or Avalanche; where no chain is named every one
      of them is searched rather than one being assumed. It reports confirmed,
      reverted, pending or not found, with the sender and recipient, value moved,
      total fee, the base fee and whether it was burned, confirmations, gas used,
      block number, any contract
      deployed and the count of ERC-20 transfers in the receipt. An address is
      answered from the chain and its block explorer on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum,
      Optimism or Polygon: whether it is a contract, an externally owned account,
      or an account carrying an EIP-7702 delegation; when a contract was deployed;
      how many transactions are recorded against it; how many an account has sent;
      and when it was last active, where a recency read the index could not date is
      reported as undated rather than as inactive. On Ethereum an explorer outage
      fails over to a second index whose count is attributed and may trail the
      chain. A reverted transaction is reported as reverted, not as a failure to
      answer; an RPC or explorer that does not respond is reported as unknown rather
      than as not found, because those are different facts; and a chain this
      endpoint does not read is named as unsupported rather than answered from a
      different chain.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: hash
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The 32-byte transaction hash, 0x followed by 64 hex characters. Omit it for a question about an address."
          - name: chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "One of ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc or avalanche. When absent, a chain named in the question is used, and otherwise every chain is searched for a hash."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. A hash or an address, the chain, and what is asked about the address are read from it."

  - path: /cve
    external_path: /cve
    method: GET
    intents: [CVE_LOOKUP]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the severity and affected versions of
      CVE-2021-44228?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      cve_id, severity, cvss_score, cvss_version, scored_by, affected_product,
      affected_versions, other_products_affected, cwe, status, published, description,
      source, source_url.
      Vulnerabilities from the National Vulnerability Database, asked three ways.
      By CVE identifier: the severity rating and CVSS base score with the CVSS
      version and the source that assigned it, the affected product and versions
      resolved from the record's CPE configuration — exact versions and half-open
      ranges alike — and what the flaw is. By year or severity, such as "critical
      CVEs 2025" or "latest CVEs": the vulnerabilities published in a stated window
      of at most 120 days with the highest-scored named, where a severity band is
      applied to each record's own CVSS base score rather than to the database's
      severity flag. By product and vulnerability class, such as "Forgejo remote
      code execution": the matching record and the fixed release where one is
      documented, used only when the record names the product asked about. A
      record with no CVSS score yet is reported as unscored rather than given an
      invented severity; a REJECTED identifier is reported as rejected rather than
      as not found; a truncated identifier is named as incomplete; and a
      rate-limited or unreachable database is reported as unknown, never as a
      vulnerability that does not exist.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: cve_id
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The CVE identifier, e.g. CVE-2024-3094. Omit it for a question by year, severity or product."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. An identifier, a year, a severity such as critical, or a product and vulnerability class are read from it."

  - path: /news-search
    external_path: /news-search
    method: GET
    intents: [NEWS_SEARCH]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Latest news about the EU AI Act", "What happened with Boeing
      this week?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      subject, window_days, articles, count.
      News article coverage of a topic, entity or time period, searched rather
      than browsed. Returns individual articles — each with its headline, the
      publisher that ran it and its publication date, most relevant first — for a
      subject read from the question, over a window the question may state
      ("in the last 3 days", "this month"). A recency word with no explicit
      window is treated as a request rather than a filter: the last 30 days are
      searched first and the search is widened only if nothing on the subject was
      published in them, and the answer says when that happened. Articles that
      are not about the subject are dropped rather than used as padding, with the
      acronym of a named entity counted as naming it. This is article coverage;
      a plain list of current headlines is /headlines. A news index that does not
      respond is reported as unknown, never as an absence of coverage.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The subject to search for: a topic, company, person or event. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: days
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Only return articles published within this many days. Read from the question when absent; omitted means no date restriction."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The subject and the time window are read from it."

  - path: /convert
    external_path: /convert
    method: GET
    intents: [CURRENCY_EXCHANGE]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Convert 100 USD to EUR", "What is 5,000 yen in dollars?".
      Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and from, to, amount,
      rate, converted, kind, as_of.
      An exchange rate, or an amount converted between two currencies. The
      primary source is the European Central Bank's euro foreign exchange
      reference rate, which is published once per day and therefore does not move
      between reads; the answer states that it is a reference rate and the date it
      was published for, so it is never mistaken for a live trading quote. The
      rate is given in both directions and the conversion direction is taken from
      the question, including the "how many X is Y" phrasing that names the target
      first. Currencies the ECB does not publish fall back to a market rate, and
      that answer says it is a market rate instead. A request naming only one
      currency is refused rather than half-answered, and a source that does not
      respond is reported as unknown rather than as a rate of zero.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: from
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "ISO 4217 code of the currency being converted from, e.g. USD. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: to
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "ISO 4217 code of the currency being converted to, e.g. EUR. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: amount
            type: number
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Amount to convert. Omitted means the question asks for the rate itself, and no amount is invented."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Both currencies, the direction and the amount are read from it."

  - path: /gas-price
    external_path: /gas-price
    method: GET
    intents: [GAS_PRICE]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the gas price on Ethereum right now?", "Gas on Base
      in Gwei". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and chain,
      gwei, base_fee_gwei, priority_gwei, block.
      The current transaction fee level on a named chain, read from that chain's
      own JSON-RPC. Reports the gas price in Gwei both exactly and rounded, the
      base fee and priority fee that make it up, the block the reading is from so
      the figure is checkable, and what a standard 21,000-gas transfer costs at
      that rate. This is the fee level and never the chain token's price, which is
      a different intent. Covers ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism and polygon; a
      chain outside that list is named as uncovered rather than answered with a
      different chain's fee, and an unresponsive endpoint is reported as unknown
      rather than as a fee of zero.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Chain to read: ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism or polygon. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The chain is read from it when the parameter is absent."

  - path: /financial
    external_path: /financial
    method: GET
    intents: [FINANCIAL_DATA]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is Solana's market cap and 24-hour volume?", "Apple's
      revenue and P/E from its 10-K". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason,
      checked_at and subject, name, chain, data.
      Market data and financial statistics for a coin, a token or a listed company,
      deliberately beyond a single quoted price. A coin named in words, such as
      Solana or Bitcoin, returns market capitalisation, 24-hour trading volume in
      dollars, fully diluted valuation, 24-hour range and change. A token contract
      address with its chain returns market capitalisation, 24-hour trading volume,
      fully diluted valuation and last traded price. A ticker or company name
      returns the day range, share volume, 52-week range and change against the
      previous close, with the ticker resolved from the company name where only a
      name is given. Revenue, net income and earnings per share come from the
      company's latest 10-K, and a price-to-earnings ratio is computed from the
      last traded price and the 10-K's diluted earnings per share, with both inputs
      named. A figure that could not be retrieved, such as margins, is stated as
      not retrieved rather than substituted.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: address
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Token contract address, e.g. 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913. Use with the chain named in the question."
          - name: symbol
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Ticker symbol or company name, e.g. AAPL or Apple. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The subject and chain are read from it."

  - path: /fraud-check
    external_path: /fraud-check
    method: GET
    intents: [FRAUD_DETECTION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Is 0x… a scam address?", "This email asks me to pay an
      invoice in gift cards: is it fraud?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence,
      reason, checked_at and subject, evidence, not_checked, sanctioned,
      flagged_hosts, scam_markers.
      How likely a named address, link or message is to be fraudulent, assessed
      from checks that are actually performed and named in the answer: the OFAC
      sanctioned digital-currency address listing, Cloudflare's threat-intelligence
      resolver for any domain in the text, the address's own on-chain state
      (contract, externally owned account, or an account carrying an EIP-7702
      delegation, with its transaction count and balance), and specific scam
      wording such as a request for a seed phrase, gift-card payment or changed
      banking details. A sanctions hit or a domain blocked as malware is reported
      as high risk. A clean result is reported as no indicators found among the
      checks performed, with the checks listed, and explicitly not as a statement
      that the subject is safe; a check that could not be completed is named as
      such rather than counted as clean. An academic paper named by title is
      checked against OpenAlex's retraction record, and a retraction is reported
      as high risk. No keyless source records misconduct findings, paper-mill
      membership or predatory-publisher status, so the answer names those three as
      not checked rather than implying a clean record, and a title that cannot be
      matched to one indexed work is reported as not found rather than matched
      loosely to a similar one.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: address
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Wallet address, URL, message text, or the title of an academic paper to assess. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim, including the message being asked about."

  - path: /token-holders
    external_path: /token-holders
    method: GET
    intents: [TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "How many holders does USDC have on Ethereum?". Returns
      answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and symbol, name, address,
      chain, holders, top_holder_percent.
      How many distinct addresses hold a named ERC-20 token, read from the chain's
      own transfer index via Blockscout. The token may be given as a contract
      address or as a symbol together with its chain, and where no chain is named
      every supported chain is checked rather than one being assumed, because the
      same symbol carries different holder counts on different chains. The answer
      names the contract the figure came from so it is checkable. Where the
      question also asks about concentration, the share of supply held by the
      single largest holder is reported, and where that list does not return in
      time the answer says so rather than omitting it silently. This is a headcount
      of holders and never a balance, a price, a supply figure or pool liquidity,
      each of which is a different intent. An identifier that is not a token, such
      as a CVE number, is named as such rather than searched for. Where more than
      one token on a chain shares a symbol with no dominant one among them, a
      contract address is asked for instead of one being picked. Covers ethereum,
      base, arbitrum, optimism and polygon.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: address
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "ERC-20 contract address, e.g. 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: symbol
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Token symbol, e.g. USDC. Used when no contract address is given."
          - name: chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Chain to read: ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism or polygon. Every supported chain is checked when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. Carries the chain, and whether holder concentration was also asked for."

  - path: /research
    external_path: /research
    method: GET
    intents: [RESEARCH_QUERY]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What clinical trials are testing semaglutide for
      Alzheimer's?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      subject, trials, citations.
      An answer to one research question, drawn from named sources: the
      ClinicalTrials.gov registry for trial phase, status and completion dates,
      Europe PMC for published literature, and Wikipedia for subjects that are
      neither. Every source is cited by identifier — the NCT number of a trial, the
      title, first author and year of a paper — so the answer can be checked rather
      than taken on trust, and a source is only cited when it actually names the
      subject asked about. Where the question asks about an outcome that has not
      been decided, such as whether a drug will be approved, the registered
      evidence to date is reported and the answer states plainly that no decision
      has been recorded; no outcome is predicted. Where neither index holds
      anything on the subject that is what the answer says, named as an absence in
      those indexes rather than as an absence of research. A request to combine
      findings across many sources into a synthesis is the RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS
      intent rather than this one.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The research question, verbatim. The subject and any named drug, trial or organisation are read from it."
        optional:
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The subject to research, when it is available separately from the question."

  - path: /crypto-price
    external_path: /crypto-price
    method: GET
    intents: [CRYPTO_PRICE]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the price of ETH?", "BTC price in EUR on
      2025-01-01". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and asset,
      symbol, price, quote, price_at, source, aggregate_price.
      The current or historical price of one named cryptocurrency, as a single
      quoted figure with the venue that quoted it and the UTC time of the quote.
      The current price is the last Coinbase trade where Coinbase lists the pair,
      Kraken's last trade where it does not, and CoinGecko's cross-venue aggregate
      as a cross-check or fallback; the answer says it is a live quote that moves
      between reads. The quote currency follows the question (USD by default; EUR,
      GBP, JPY, INR and other major fiat, or BTC and ETH). A dollar stablecoin's
      answer also states its distance from the one-dollar peg. A date returns that
      UTC day's Coinbase open and close and CoinGecko's daily snapshot, labelled as
      historical. This is one price, never market capitalisation or volume, which
      is FINANCIAL_DATA, and never what an address holds, which is
      WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. A fork or wrapped asset such as Bitcoin Cash, Ethereum
      Classic or Wrapped Bitcoin is priced as itself, never as the major whose name
      it contains, and a multi-word coin name is matched whole. Testnet assets are
      answered as having no market price, a future date is declined as a
      prediction, an asset name that matches no listed coin exactly is not
      substituted with a similar one, and a provider outage is reported as an
      outage rather than a missing price.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: symbol
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Asset name or ticker, e.g. ETH or Ethereum. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The asset, the quote currency and any date are read from it."

  - path: /stock-price
    external_path: /stock-price
    method: GET
    intents: [STOCK_PRICE]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is Apple's share price?", "TSLA closing price on
      2026-09-01". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and ticker,
      name, price, currency, price_at, exchange, market_open, source.
      The current or historical share price of one listed equity, given as a
      ticker or a company name. Every answer states the exchange, the quote time
      in the exchange's own time zone, and whether the regular trading session is
      open right now; outside the session the figure is labelled as the last
      session price and never presented as a live quote. A company name is
      resolved to its ticker and accepted only when the listing carries every word
      of the name asked about, so an unlisted subsidiary is answered as not found
      rather than with a related company's price. A ticker is read only when it is
      written as one in capitals, and a currency code such as (USD) is never taken
      for a ticker. A question that does not ask about a share price, such as a
      weather question naming a city, is refused rather than priced. An ISO date
      returns that day's closing price, and a date with no session is said to have
      none. A question asking whether a stock will rise or fall is answered with
      the price and an explicit statement that no forecast is made. Company
      fundamentals and statistics beyond one price are FINANCIAL_DATA. A provider
      outage, including a failed ticker search, is reported as an outage and never
      as the company not being listed.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: symbol
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Ticker in capitals, e.g. AAPL, or a company name, e.g. Apple. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The company, ticker and any ISO date are read from it."

  - path: /cross-chain
    external_path: /cross-chain
    method: GET
    intents: [CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Was LayerZero message 0x… delivered from Ethereum to
      Arbitrum?", "Did bridge transaction 0x… arrive on Base?". Returns answer,
      verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and message (guid, nonce, source_chain,
      destination_chain, sender, receiver, source_tx, destination_tx, scan_status).
      Whether a LayerZero V2 bridge message sent from one chain was executed on
      another, verified from both chains' own receipts rather than taken from an
      indexer's status. The message is located on LayerZero Scan by its source or
      destination transaction hash or its GUID; the source receipt must carry the
      endpoint's PacketSent event and the destination receipt its PacketDelivered
      event, and both must agree on nonce, sender, receiver and GUID. Answers are
      verified, not yet delivered, mismatch (including a message that travels
      between different chains than the ones asked about), or not found. Covers
      ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc and avalanche. State roots,
      Merkle-Patricia proofs and block headers are not verified cryptographically,
      and every answer to a request for one says so. Other bridges such as
      Wormhole or native rollup bridges are not checked. A nonce with no
      transaction hash, GUID or sender does not identify a message, and one is
      asked for. An RPC or indexer outage is reported as an outage.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: tx_hash
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Source or destination transaction hash, or the LayerZero message GUID, 0x-prefixed 64 hex characters. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: source_chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Chain the message was sent from, e.g. arbitrum."
          - name: destination_chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Chain the message should have executed on, e.g. base."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The reference, both chains and any nonce are read from it."

  - path: /event-outcome
    external_path: /event-outcome
    method: GET
    intents: [EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Who won the 2024 US presidential election?", "Has the
      Polymarket market on … resolved?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason,
      checked_at and outcome, winner, event, source.
      The actual outcome of a named, checkable event, as settled by a public
      prediction market, for a market or conditional contract to resolve against.
      Polymarket's real-money markets and Manifold's play-money markets are
      searched, and a market is used only when it carries every name and number
      in the question, asks about the same move (a cut, a rise or no change), and
      is mostly about that event, so a market on a different subject or the
      opposite proposition that shares most of the words is not used. A settled
      market is reported with its settled outcome and the market's own wording,
      and a Manifold settlement is labelled as play money. An unsettled market is
      reported as unresolved with its scheduled close, and its trading odds are
      never given as an outcome. Nothing is predicted: a request for an opinion or
      forecast is declined by name, and a question that names no specific event is
      asked to name one. Where no matching market exists the answer says so;
      official sources such as flight trackers, election authorities and league
      results are not read. A provider outage is reported as an outage.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: event
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The event to resolve, e.g. Fed rate decision at the September 2025 meeting. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The event, its names, numbers and dates are read from it."

  - path: /url-scan
    external_path: /url-scan
    method: GET
    intents: [URL_SCAN]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Is https://example.com/offer safe to click?". Returns
      answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and url, flagged_by, checks.
      A safe or unsafe verdict on one URL, with the evidence behind it named.
      The host is resolved through Cloudflare's malware-and-phishing filtering
      resolver and compared with an unfiltered resolver, so a block is reported
      only when the filter answers 0.0.0.0 for a name that really resolves; Quad9
      threat-blocking DNS is compared with its unfiltered resolver the same way; the
      host and exact URL are looked up in URLhaus's current malware lists; the TLS
      certificate is inspected; and the redirect chain is walked hop by hop, each
      hop checked to be a public address before it is contacted. A listing makes
      a URL unsafe. A brand name used on a domain that is not a known domain of
      that brand, punycode, a bare IP address or an invalid certificate makes it
      suspicious. With none of those, and only when both the filtering resolver
      and URLhaus answered, the URL is reported as appearing safe, and the answer
      says plainly that no blocklist can prove a site safe. A host that does not
      resolve is reported as unreachable. When either threat source does not
      answer, that is reported as an outage and never as a safe verdict. A
      question only about a certificate is SSL_VERIFICATION and is refused by
      name, and a list of which engines flag a URL is URL_SAFE.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: url
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The URL to scan, e.g. https://example.com/offer. A bare host is read as https. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim, including the URL when it is not sent separately."

  - path: /web-search
    external_path: /web-search
    method: GET
    intents: [WEB_SEARCH]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the latest news on the Fed's rate decision?", "Who
      is the CEO of OpenAI?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at
      and articles, background.
      Current, externally sourced information for a question that static
      knowledge cannot answer, taken from Google News search and, when no current
      report exists, from Wikipedia. The answer quotes the most relevant reports'
      headlines with publisher and publication date, so every clause can be
      checked; nothing is paraphrased by a model. A report is only cited when it
      names the subject, and when the question names a product or trial code such
      as MK-2870 the headline must name that code. A question about a future
      outcome is answered with the current coverage and states that it is not a
      prediction. A TLS certificate check, a scholarly literature search, a
      single CVE record or a request to explain a concept from static knowledge
      is refused by name as the intent it belongs to. When the sources that
      answered find nothing on the subject, that is reported as an absence in
      those sources only; when Google News does not answer, that is reported as an
      outage.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The question, verbatim. The subject, any named organisation and any product or trial code are read from it."
        optional:
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The subject to search for, when it is available separately from the question."

  - path: /sentiment
    external_path: /sentiment
    method: GET
    intents: [SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "What is the sentiment of this review: 'The product broke
      after one day'?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      compound, positive_words, negative_words, tones.
      The sentiment a supplied text expresses — positive, negative, neutral or
      mixed — read by a hosted open-weight language model called over the
      network, which writes the label and a short explanation. When that model does
      not answer within its time budget the text is read instead with a rule-based
      word list and the VADER method (negation, intensifiers, a contrastive "but",
      capitals and exclamation marks), and everything below describes that fallback. A negation reaches at most three words
      forward and never across a comma or full stop, so "No problems, great
      service" reads as positive. The answer names the words that carried the
      label, so it can be checked against the text, and names an emotional tone
      such as frustrated or joyful only when a word in the text states it and is
      not negated. A text with no opinion word is reported as neutral with that
      reason given. Sarcasm, irony and opinion words outside the list are not
      detected, so a neutral reading can be a miss. Assigning a text to
      caller-supplied categories is TEXT_CLASSIFICATION rather than this intent. A
      request with no text is refused by name rather than scored.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: text
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The passage whose sentiment is asked about, exactly as given. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim, including the quoted passage when it is not sent separately."

  - path: /classify
    external_path: /classify
    method: GET
    intents: [TEXT_CLASSIFICATION]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Classify this ticket as billing, technical or account: 'I
      was charged twice'". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and
      label.
      Assigns a supplied text to one of the labels the request itself supplies,
      such as billing, technical or account issue. There is no fixed taxonomy. A hosted open-weight language model called over
      the network chooses among the supplied labels and explains the choice in a
      sentence or two; a label outside the supplied set is discarded. When that
      model does not answer within its time budget, everything below applies
      instead: a label wins on lexical relatedness, when a label word appears in
      the text or when text and label words are neighbours in the keyless Datamuse
      word index, and the answer names the words that matched so the choice can be
      checked. When no label clears the runner-up by a clear margin the text is
      reported as ambiguous between them rather than a label being guessed, and a
      negated label such as "not spam" is never chosen merely because evidence for
      the other is absent. Label sets of positive, negative and neutral are read
      with the sentiment word list instead. Where the word index does not respond,
      only direct label-word matches are counted and the answer says so; an
      ambiguity reached that way is reported as a source outage. Emotional tone on
      its own is SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS. A request without a label set or without text
      is refused by name.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: text
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The passage to classify, exactly as given. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: labels
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The candidate labels as a comma-separated list, e.g. billing, technical, account issue. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim, including the labels and the quoted passage when they are not sent separately."

  - path: /research-synthesis
    external_path: /research-synthesis
    method: GET
    intents: [RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Summarise the evidence on intermittent fasting and weight
      loss". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and sources.
      Findings on a topic gathered across several published studies and combined
      into one answer. PubMed and Europe PMC are searched on title and abstract,
      and from each study a single sentence reporting a result is quoted verbatim
      from its abstract and attributed by first author, year and PubMed id. A
      sentence is quoted only when it states a result, such as an association, a
      reduction or a conclusion, and when every topic word appears as a whole word
      in it or in the study's title. Statements of purpose ("To examine ..."),
      search and methods descriptions, definitions, background attributed to
      earlier work and calls for further research are never quoted as findings.
      Nothing is generated, and whether the studies agree is explicitly not
      assessed. Requests for the latest or recent studies are limited to the last
      five years. When the request supplies its own notes, on separate lines or run
      together on one line, they are restated grouped by source with their
      attributions kept, nothing is fetched, and a stated topic that no note
      addresses is named as unaddressed. Where only one study yields a quotable
      finding the answer says no synthesis across sources was possible; where both
      indexes fail that is reported as an outage and never as an absence of
      research. A cited answer to one narrow question is RESEARCH_QUERY rather than
      this intent.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original request, verbatim, including any notes to be summarised."
          - name: topic
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The subject to synthesise, e.g. intermittent fasting, when it is available separately from the request."

  - path: /fact-check
    external_path: /fact-check
    method: GET
    intents: [FACT_CHECK]
    description: >-
      Example questions: "Is it true that the Eiffel Tower is in Paris?", "Fact-check:
      water boils at 100 °C at sea level". Returns answer, verdict, confidence,
      reason, checked_at and claim, source, source_url, evidence.
      A specific claim, looked up against a citable encyclopaedic reference and
      reported with the article named and quoted. Reports an explicit refutation when
      the source states one, and otherwise says plainly that the source does not settle
      the claim. It does not adjudicate contested claims and never asserts that a claim
      is true on the strength of a topical match.
    params:
      query:
        required:
          - name: claim
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The claim to check, e.g. The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris."
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The claim is extracted from it."

  - path: /sanctions-screen
    external_path: /sanctions-screen
    method: GET
    intents: [SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH]
    description: >-
      Screens a person, company or wallet against the OFAC SDN list and the UN
      Security Council Consolidated List, read live, including every listed alias
      and near-matches on spelling or transliteration. Example questions: "Screen
      'Ivan Petrov, DOB 1974, Cyprus' against the OFAC SDN list", "Is Viktor But
      sanctioned?", "Is wallet 0x… on a sanctions list?". A birth year in the
      question is checked against the listed ones. Returns verdict (match,
      possible_match, no_match or unknown), confidence, matches (up to five, each
      with list, reference id, listed name, the name or alias that matched,
      type, programmes, score 0-1, listed birth years, whether the birth year
      agrees, nationalities, listing date and the OFAC record URL), closest (the
      nearest entry when nothing matched), lists_checked (each list with its
      published date and entry count) and lists_not_checked. The EU and UK lists
      are not screened and the answer says so. A name match alone never
      establishes identity, and the answer says that too.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: name
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Person or company to screen, e.g. Ivan Petrov or Banco Nacional de Cuba. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: wallet
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "A crypto wallet address to screen against OFAC's listed digital currency addresses."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. A birth year and whether the subject is a person or a company are read from it."

  - path: /company-registry
    external_path: /company-registry
    method: GET
    intents: [CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP]
    description: >-
      A company's official register record, read live from the GLEIF LEI
      register and, for a US filer, SEC EDGAR. Example questions: "What is the
      incorporation status and registered agent for Tesla, Inc.?", "Is Barclays
      Bank PLC still registered?", "UK company number 01026167", "Look up LEI
      5493001KJTIIGC8Y1R12". Returns verdict (found, not_found or unknown),
      legal_name, lei, entity_status (ACTIVE or INACTIVE), lei_registration_status,
      jurisdiction, legal_form, company_number and the register that issued it
      (Companies House, a US Secretary of State, …), registered_address,
      registered_agent when the registered address is an agent's, headquarters_address,
      incorporated, other_names, direct_parent and ultimate_parent (name and LEI),
      us_filer (CIK, state of incorporation, industry code, addresses and former
      names from EDGAR), other_candidates with similar names, and sources.
      Directors and beneficial owners are in neither source, and every answer
      says so instead of leaving them out silently.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: company
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Company name, e.g. Tesla, Inc. or Revolut Ltd, or a 20-character LEI. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: company_number
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The number the company is registered under, e.g. UK company number 01026167."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. A country named in it, such as UK or Delaware, narrows the search."

  - path: /sec-filings
    external_path: /sec-filings
    method: GET
    intents: [REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR]
    description: >-
      Whether an issuer has filed a statutory filing on SEC EDGAR, when it was
      accepted, and what it reports, read live from the issuer's own EDGAR
      filing index. Example questions: "Has Tesla filed its latest 10-Q on SEC
      EDGAR, on what date was it accepted, and what did it disclose about
      margins?", "Did Apple file an 8-K in the last 30 days?", "What is
      Microsoft's most recent filing?". Covers 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 6-K, 40-F,
      S-1, DEF 14A and amendments. Returns verdict (filed, not_filed, not_found or
      unknown), company, cik, tickers, filing (form, filed date, EDGAR acceptance
      time in UTC, accession number, period or event date, 8-K items with their
      names, and the document URL), recent_filings (up to five), and for a 10-Q,
      10-K or 20-F the figures tagged in that filing's XBRL: revenue, gross
      profit, gross margin, operating income and net income for its period, with
      prior_year_figures for the same period a year earlier. Only SEC EDGAR is
      read; a question about another regulator says that it is not covered.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: company
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Issuer name or ticker, e.g. Tesla or TSLA. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: form
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Form type, e.g. 10-Q, 10-K or 8-K. Read from the question when absent; \"annual report\" means 10-K."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. A window such as \"in the last 30 days\" or \"since 2026-09-01\" is read from it."

  - path: /transfer-verify
    external_path: /transfer-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [CRYPTO_TRANSFER_VERIFY]
    description: >-
      Verifies one on-chain transfer by hash, read from public JSON-RPC on
      Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain or Avalanche, with
      every chain searched when none is named. Example questions: "Verify transfer
      0x…: did it succeed, who sent it to whom, how much fee was burned and how
      many confirmations does it have?". Returns verdict (confirmed, reverted,
      pending, not_found or unknown) and a transaction object with status, from,
      to, value_wei, value, symbol, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status,
      method, gas_used, fee_wei, confirmations, base_fee_wei and base_fee_burned:
      true on Ethereum and Polygon, where the EIP-1559 base fee is burned, false
      on rollups, where it is paid to the sequencer, and null before London or
      when the block could not be read. Confirmations are counted from the chain
      head at the time of the answer.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: hash
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The 32-byte transaction hash, 0x followed by 64 hex characters."
          - name: chain
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc or avalanche. Every chain is searched when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim. The hash and chain are read from it when the parameters are absent."

  - path: /macro
    external_path: /macro
    method: GET
    intents: [MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR]
    description: >-
      The latest released value of a macroeconomic statistic, read from the agency
      that publishes it. Example questions: "What was the latest US CPI
      year-over-year print, and what is the current federal funds target range?",
      "What is euro area inflation and the ECB deposit rate?", "What is the
      unemployment rate in Germany?", "What was Japan's GDP growth last year?".
      US CPI, core CPI and unemployment come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics,
      monthly, with CPI computed year on year from the index; the federal funds
      target range and effective rate from the New York Fed, daily; euro area and
      EU inflation (HICP) and unemployment from Eurostat, monthly; ECB deposit and
      main refinancing rates from the ECB, daily; other countries' inflation,
      unemployment and GDP from the World Bank, annual and labelled annual. Returns
      verdict (reported, not_covered or unknown), region and indicators, each with
      value (and value_high for a range), unit, period, frequency, series id,
      source and source_url. Several statistics can be asked for at once. A policy
      rate outside the US and the euro area is named as not covered rather than
      replaced by another figure.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: indicator
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The statistic, e.g. CPI, core inflation, unemployment, policy rate or GDP growth. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: country
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "Country or region, e.g. US, euro area, Germany or Japan. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim."

  - path: /url-reputation
    external_path: /url-reputation
    method: GET
    intents: [URL_SAFE]
    description: >-
      Whether a URL or domain is listed as malicious, and by which sources, read
      live from three keyless threat sources: Cloudflare security DNS and Quad9
      threat-blocking DNS (each compared with an unfiltered resolver, so a block is
      reported only for a name that really resolves) and abuse.ch URLhaus, matched
      on the exact URL and on the host. Example questions: "Check
      https://login-secure-update.example.com against threat feeds and DNS
      blocklists: is it listed for phishing, and by which engines?", "Is
      malware.testcategory.com on any blocklist?". Returns verdict, listed (true,
      false, or null when a source did not answer), sources (each with source,
      kind, result listed, not_listed, unknown, unavailable or not_applicable, and
      whether URLhaus matched the exact URL or the host), flagged_by, and the
      underlying checks: TLS certificate, lookalike markers, whether the host
      resolves, redirect count and final URL. A clean listing is never called
      proof of safety.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: url
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The URL or domain to check, e.g. https://login-secure-update.example.com. Read from the question when absent."
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The user's original question, verbatim."

  - path: /answer
    external_path: /answer
    method: GET
    intents: [QUESTION_ANSWERING]
    description: >-
      Answers an open-domain question, or a question about a passage supplied with
      it, with every factual claim cited to a numbered source. Example questions:
      "Who won the 2022 FIFA World Cup and where was it held?", "Why is the sky
      blue?", "Based on the following text: … When did the war end?". Open-domain
      sources are up to five English Wikipedia article introductions, found by
      searching the question, its keywords and its subject phrase; a supplied
      passage is the only source when one is given. A free model phrases the answer
      from those sources only, and the reply is kept only if every sentence cites a
      source that exists; otherwise the answer is the source sentence that best
      matches the question, quoted and cited. Returns verdict (answered,
      not_in_sources or unknown), method (model_phrased_from_sources or
      extracted_from_sources), and citations (number, title, URL and kind for each
      source). When the sources do not contain the answer it says so instead of
      guessing.
    params:
      query:
        optional:
          - name: query
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "The question, verbatim. A passage may be included: \"Context: … Question: …\" or \"Based on the following text: … ?\"."
          - name: context
            type: string
            intents: ["*"]
            description: "A passage to answer from. When given, it is the only source."

# input_schema is a single top-level block covering every endpoint — the schema
# refuses it inside endpoints[], and the node does not enforce it against requests.
input_schema:
  type: object
  description: >-
    Telegraph's engine fills the parameters a miner declares here and does not
    pass the rest of the question, so anything not declared is invisible. The
    query field is declared first because it carries the wording the structured
    fields cannot — an explicit start date, a time window, a wind threshold.
  properties:
    query:
      type: string
      description: >-
        The user's original question, verbatim. Preferred over the structured
        fields: it carries detail they cannot, such as "starting next Monday",
        "in 44 hours", or "flag winds above 25 knots".
      examples:
        - "What is the storm risk at latitude 12.97, longitude 77.59 in 44 hours?"
        - "Can you analyze the TLS certificate chain and hostname match for api.github.com?"
    q:
      type: string
      description: Alias for query.
    name:
      type: string
      description: Person or company to screen for sanctions, e.g. Ivan Petrov.
    wallet:
      type: string
      description: Crypto wallet address to screen against OFAC's listed digital currency addresses.
    company:
      type: string
      description: Company name or LEI for a register lookup, e.g. Tesla, Inc.
    company_number:
      type: string
      description: The number a company is registered under, e.g. UK company number 01026167.
    form:
      type: string
      description: SEC form type for a filing check, e.g. 10-Q, 10-K or 8-K.
    indicator:
      type: string
      description: A macroeconomic statistic, e.g. CPI, unemployment, policy rate or GDP growth.
    country:
      type: string
      description: Country or region for a macroeconomic statistic, e.g. US, euro area or Japan.
    domain:
      type: string
      description: >-
        /ssl-check. Hostname to check. Accepts "example.com",
        "https://example.com/path", or "example.com:8443".
      examples: ["example.com", "expired.badssl.com"]
    location:
      type: string
      description: >-
        /storm-alert and /weather-forecast. Place name, e.g. "Chennai" or
        "Tokyo, Japan".
      examples: ["Chennai", "Tokyo, Japan"]
    latitude:
      type: number
      description: >-
        /storm-alert and /weather-forecast. Use with longitude when the question
        names coordinates rather than a place.
      minimum: -90
      maximum: 90
    longitude:
      type: number
      minimum: -180
      maximum: 180
    lat:
      type: number
      description: Alias for latitude.
    lon:
      type: number
      description: Alias for longitude.
    hours:
      type: integer
      description: >-
        /storm-alert and /weather-forecast. Forecast window in hours. Also read
        from the question itself, e.g. "over the next 44 hours".
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 384
    forecast_hours:
      type: integer
      description: Alias for hours.
    days:
      type: integer
      description: Forecast span in days, converted to hours.
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 16
    forecast_days:
      type: integer
      description: Alias for days.
    topic:
      type: string
      description: /papers. Research subject to search for, e.g. "zero knowledge proofs".
    ip:
      type: string
      description: /ip-geolocate. IPv4 or IPv6 address.
      examples: ["8.8.8.8"]
    text:
      type: string
      description: >-
        /translate and /ai-detect. The text to translate, or the passage whose
        authorship is to be analysed, with or without quotes. Registration
        260 declared no translation-shaped parameter and both scored epochs
        arrived with none filled — the engine fills only parameters a miner
        declares, so this field is what makes translation questions reach us.
      examples: ["The weather is beautiful today."]
    target_language:
      type: string
      description: >-
        /translate. The language to translate into, by name or ISO 639-1 code.
      examples: ["Spanish", "fr"]
    source_language:
      type: string
      description: /translate. The language of the source text, when stated.
      examples: ["English"]

output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    domain: { type: string }
    chain_length:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: Certificates the server presented, leaf included. /ssl-check only.
    chain_complete:
      type: [boolean, "null"]
      description: Whether intermediates were sent, not just the leaf.
    subject_alt_names:
      type: [array, "null"]
      items: { type: string }
      description: Subject Alternative Names on the leaf certificate.
    unreachable_reason:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: Why the host could not be reached, when it could not be.
    start_time:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: >-
        First hour of the returned series, UTC. /weather-forecast honours an
        explicit start named in the question.
    end_time:
      type: [string, "null"]
    hourly_count:
      type: integer
      description: Number of hourly values returned.
    hourly_min_precipitation_mm:
      type: [number, "null"]
    hourly_max_precipitation_mm:
      type: [number, "null"]
    time_mode:
      type: string
      description: >-
        "point" when the question asked about one moment ("in 44 hours", "right
        now"); "window" when it asked about a span ("over the next 44 hours").
      enum: [point, window]
    valid_at:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: >-
        For a point answer, the UTC hour the values describe. Null for a window.
    risk_score:
      type: number
      description: >-
        Storm risk from 0 (none) to 1 (severe). /storm-alert only.
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
    verdict:
      type: string
      description: >-
        The answer's label, and its vocabulary is per endpoint. /ssl-check returns a
        certificate state (valid, expired, not_yet_valid, hostname_mismatch,
        self_signed, untrusted, unreachable); /storm-alert a storm-risk grade (none,
        low, moderate, high, severe); /weather-forecast a condition (clear, mostly
        clear, cloudy, fog, drizzle, rain, heavy rain, snow, thunderstorms);
        /translate "translated"; /papers "papers"; /ai-detect likely_human, likely_ai
        or inconclusive; and /ip-geolocate the resolved place itself, or the class of
        a special-use range (private, reserved, loopback, link_local, shared,
        multicast, broadcast). Any endpoint returns "unknown" when it could not
        answer. A closed enum was declared here previously and four endpoints did not
        conform to it, /ip-geolocate least of all because a place name cannot be
        enumerated.
    valid: { type: boolean }
    trusted: { type: boolean }
    expired: { type: boolean }
    hostname_match: { type: boolean }
    issuer: { type: [string, "null"] }
    subject: { type: [string, "null"] }
    valid_from: { type: [string, "null"] }
    valid_to: { type: [string, "null"] }
    days_remaining: { type: [integer, "null"] }
    tls_protocol: { type: [string, "null"] }
    confidence: { type: number }
    reason: { type: string }
    checked_at: { type: string }
    location: { type: [string, "null"] }
    storm_expected: { type: boolean }
    max_wind_gust_kmh: { type: [number, "null"] }
    max_wind_speed_kmh: { type: [number, "null"] }
    max_precipitation_mm: { type: [number, "null"] }
    thunderstorm: { type: boolean }
    window_hours: { type: [integer, "null"] }
    peak_at: { type: [string, "null"] }
    latitude: { type: [number, "null"] }
    longitude: { type: [number, "null"] }
    temp_min_c: { type: [number, "null"] }
    temp_max_c: { type: [number, "null"] }
    total_precipitation_mm: { type: [number, "null"] }
    precipitation_hours: { type: [integer, "null"] }

    # Everything below was returned by a live endpoint but described nowhere, on
    # nine of the ten routes. Nothing enforces this schema — there is no required
    # list, additionalProperties is not false, and our IP answers scored 0.9920
    # while violating the verdict enum that used to be here — so this was never a
    # functional fault. It is the same inaccuracy that enum was, and it is fixed
    # in the same signature rather than left to describe a service we stopped
    # being.

    # /storm-alert
    wind_direction: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Compass direction of the peak wind." }
    threshold_exceeded: { type: [boolean, "null"], description: "Whether a wind threshold named in the question was crossed." }
    threshold_hours: { type: [array, "null"], items: { type: string }, description: "The UTC hours at which it was crossed." }

    # /weather-forecast
    precipitation_probability_max_pct: { type: [number, "null"] }
    span_days: { type: [integer, "null"], description: "Forecast span in days when the question asked in days." }

    # /ip-geolocate. `verdict` carries the resolved place, so these are its parts.
    ip: { type: [string, "null"] }
    city: { type: [string, "null"] }
    region: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Subdivision for an IP; requested news region for /headlines." }
    country: { type: [string, "null"] }
    country_code: { type: [string, "null"] }
    timezone: { type: [string, "null"] }
    asn: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Autonomous system number of the announcing network." }
    organisation: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Network operator the address is registered to." }

    # /translate. `reason` is the bare translation; this repeats it explicitly.
    translation: { type: [string, "null"] }

    # /papers
    papers:
      type: [array, "null"]
      description: "Each entry carries title, authors, year, citations, venue and doi."
      items:
        type: object
        properties:
          title: { type: string }
          year: { type: [integer, "null"] }
          authors: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          citations: { type: [integer, "null"] }
          venue: { type: [string, "null"] }
          doi: { type: [string, "null"] }
    topic: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Subject actually searched for, after parsing the question." }
    from_date: { type: [string, "null"] }
    to_date: { type: [string, "null"] }
    count: { type: [integer, "null"], description: "Number of papers or headlines returned." }

    # /ai-detect. The measurements behind the verdict, so a reader can disagree
    # with it — the confidence is deliberately low and these are why.
    words: { type: [integer, "null"] }
    sentences: { type: [integer, "null"] }
    mean_sentence_words: { type: [number, "null"] }
    sentence_length_stdev: { type: [number, "null"] }
    type_token_ratio: { type: [number, "null"] }
    repeated_bigrams: { type: [integer, "null"] }
    formulaic_markers: { type: [array, "null"], items: { type: string } }

    # /extract
    extracted:
      type: [object, "null"]
      description: "The fields the question asked for. Keys vary with the request — emails, phones, urls, quantities, dates, entities, action items."

    # /headlines
    headlines:
      type: [array, "null"]
      items:
        type: object
        properties:
          title: { type: string }
          source: { type: [string, "null"] }
          published: { type: [string, "null"] }

    # /wallet-balance
    # /fact-check
    claim: { type: [string, "null"] }
    source: { type: [string, "null"], description: "The reference consulted, named so a reader can weigh it." }
    source_url: { type: [string, "null"] }
    evidence: { type: [string, "null"], description: "The passage the verdict was read from." }

    # /wallet-balance
    address: { type: [string, "null"] }
    chain: { type: [string, "null"], description: "ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism or polygon." }
    balance_eth: { type: [number, "null"], description: "Native-coin balance. Null when the RPC did not answer, which is not the same as zero." }
    symbol: { type: [string, "null"], description: "Native coin of the chain — POL on polygon, ETH elsewhere." }

docs:
  repository: https://github.com/Harshyadav442277/miner

# Explicit, and matching the pinned YAML of registration 236, which is the only
# configuration this miner has ever been accepted under. No API key exists
# anywhere in this service, so nothing upstream can revoke us. Keep the console's
# "REQUIRES API KEY" toggle OFF, which produces exactly this block.
auth:
  type: none

rate_limit_per_sec: 20
cache_ttl_sec: 60
circuit_threshold: 5
circuit_cooldown_seconds: 30
